market_view: The market is stressed. The VIX fear gauge is at 25.6, credit spreads are widening, and the S&P 500 is only about 1% above its 200-day average after its worst week since June. Democrats swept the midterms, which hit AI-infrastructure stocks (new limits on data-center building) and defense stocks (Trump's $1.5T defense budget looks doomed). On Thursday the Nasdaq fell about 5.5% and chip stocks about 12%; Friday won back only part of that. October jobs came in hot (+165k against about 60k expected), pushing December rate-hike odds to about 77%. That means October CPI on Nov 10 can move the market sharply in either direction. The portfolio already leans defensive: healthcare, consumer staples, Walmart, Treasuries and modest defense stocks, with little tech or chip exposure. So this is a day to hold, not to chase rebounds or add risk before CPI.
